chunks: There are some among them who listen to you; but We have put a covering on their hearts so that they fail to understand it, and a deafness appears in their ears. Even if they saw all the signs they would not believe in them; and even when they come to you to dispute with you, the unbelievers say: "This is nothing but fables of antiquity."

key_terms.أَسَاطِيرُ: fables or ancient tales (plural of أَسْطُورَة)
key_terms.وَقْرًا: deafness or dullness in the ears
key_terms.يَفْقَهُوهُ: they understand it (from فقه, deep understanding)

ai.seo_question: Why do some people listen to the Quran but fail to understand or believe in it?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the interplay between divine decree and human agency, where persistent rejection of truth hardens the heart, creating a spiritual barrier (akinnah) that prevents deep comprehension. The dismissal of the Quran as 'asatir al-awwalin' (fables of the ancients) reflects a cognitive dissonance where disbelievers rationalize their refusal to accept the Prophet's message despite clear evidence. This state of 'deafness' is not merely physical but a consequence of their own choices, illustrating the principle of 'takhattum' (sealing) of the heart due to repeated denial.
